title: Creation of HBSS Wash Buffer
author: Brusko Laboratory
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8xbhxin

steps.title: Open sterile filter unit
steps.instruction: Open a sterile 1 L Rapid‑Flow Sterile Disposable Filter Unit equipped with a 0.2 µm PES membrane (Nalgene, part 5670020).

steps.title: Add reagents and filter
steps.instruction: Add HBSS, FBS, Pen/Strep, and EDTA to the filter unit, then filter the mixture through the 0.2 µm PES membrane using a positive‑pressure system.

substeps.instruction: Add 940 mL of 1× HBSS (Gibco, catalog #14175‑095) to the filter flask.
Add a single 50 mL aliquot of fetal bovine serum (Genesee Scientific, catalog #25‑550).
Add a 10 mL aliquot of Penicillin/Streptomycin (Corning, catalog #30‑002‑CL).
Add 10 µL of 0.5 M EDTA (Boston Bioproducts, catalog #BM‑150).
Process the final solution through the 0.2 µm PES membrane using a positive‑pressure system.

steps.title: Dispose of used filter
steps.instruction: Once filtration is complete, unscrew and remove the filter from the flask and discard it in biohazard waste, following antibiotic‑containing waste disposal guidelines.

steps.title: Seal, label, and store buffer
steps.instruction: Remove the secondary container lid, securely screw the cap onto the flask, label the flask with “HBSS with FBS, EDTA, Pen/Strep”, your name and the date, and store the HBSS Wash Buffer at 4 °C.
